partial_progress.details: Phase 14 (Add Class, Tag and Cost-Class Selection to run-all.sh) closed [COMPLETED]. Added --class CLASS[,...], --tag TAG[,...], --cost-class CLASS[,...] to tests/run-all.sh, each opt-in and composing with --only and with each other by intersection. Zero new per-suite hand-authoring: --class reads the existing suite-classification.data column; --tag is mechanically derived from that same file's invokes:X[,Y] reason tokens plus a fixed 'lint' tag for test-lint-*.sh; --cost-class buckets the existing suite-cost-hints.txt wall_ms column at fixed thresholds (free, moderate, slow, unknown). The six new selection/derivation functions live in scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh as additive functions; every pre-existing function and the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel are untouched. Extended test-run-all-selection.sh with 12 new cases (14-25): 4 library-level correctness cases against the real corpus and 8 run-all.sh flag-level cases (selection, refuse-loudly-on-unknown-value, AND-composition) against a dedicated fixture -- all 31 cases pass. Confirmed --only/--jobs/--timings/--fail-on-new remain byte-identical absent the new flags via a direct diff against the pre-change file. Documented the new selectors in shell-script-testing.md. NET-PROD +318 (run-all.sh +121/-1, suite-selection-lib.sh +198/-0), NET-TEST +175 (test-run-all-selection.sh, fully additive), both net-positive and pre-justified in the plan as the mechanism that keeps the corpus from re-growing. The Tier Justification's literal verification command (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 8) is a documented no-op (SKIP, since --skip-slow defers gate 8 entirely); real coverage came from a direct, unbounded verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 8 run and a direct run-all.sh --quiet full-battery run on the live, redeployed corpus: 168/175 passed, 7 failed (2 EXPECTED, 5 NEW), none of which reference any file this phase touched -- logged via issue-record.sh as host-state-contention (multiple concurrent sibling orchestrate cycles were live throughout this session), not treated as a regression. A separate transient gate10 timeout on one of two --skip-slow deploy verification runs was confirmed non-reproducing on immediate re-run. 6 of 20 plan phases remain [NOT STARTED] (Phase 15 next). Clean phase boundary, not a context-exhaustion handoff.

memory_candidates.content: When a test corpus's existing per-suite declarative data file already records WHY a suite is classified a certain way (e.g. an 'invokes:X,Y' reason column for an integration-class suite), a new free-form 'tag' selection axis can be mechanically derived from that existing column plus one or two fixed basename rules, with ZERO new per-suite hand-authoring. This is strictly preferable to retrofitting a new tag column across the whole corpus by hand: a bulk hand-authored retrofit is itself a net-line-count cost and an error-prone one-time snapshot that drifts, while a mechanical derivation always reflects the live corpus and costs nothing to keep current.

In this Claude Code sandbox environment, a foreground Bash tool call is auto-backgrounded by the harness after approximately 180 seconds of execution REGARDLESS of the Bash tool's own requested `timeout` parameter value (observed at timeout=590000 and 430000, both still cut at ~180s). A true single-call 'block until the wait resolves' bounded-waiter idiom is therefore not achievable past ~180s in this environment. The workable substitute: explicitly `nohup cmd > log 2>&1 & disown` to obtain a real, independently-pollable PID outside the harness's own backgrounding path, then issue repeated SHORT (<180s) `kill -0 "$pid"` liveness-check calls one at a time (each its own tool call) until the process exits, then read the log file directly. Do not assume a single long-`timeout` foreground call will actually block for its full stated duration in this environment.
